title: How many times thicker does the paper get over two folds?
description: The thickness table of the folded sheet is used to divide a later thickness by an earlier one, over two folds, three folds and ten folds. Keeko's doubt is that two folds make the paper only two times as thick.
teaching_notes: One idea: the growth over any stretch of folds is two multiplied by itself once for every fold in the stretch, wherever the stretch starts. Watch for students who think two folds make the paper two times as thick.

source: Check that two folds multiply the thickness by 4, three fold
video_script.why: The child has the thickness table and now sees how much the thickness grows over a few folds, wherever they start.
video_script.substitution: The book's own thickness table, with later thicknesses divided by earlier ones.
video_script.anchor: the book's thickness table for the folded sheet, with two rows lit up at a time
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks two folds make the paper two times as thick. The second fold doubles the thickness the first fold already doubled, so two folds multiply by two and then by two again.
video_script.payoff_line: Every ten folds multiply the thickness by one thousand and twenty four

final_answer.value: Every 2 folds multiply by 4, every 3 by 8 and every 10 by 1024
final_answer.spoken: every two folds multiply by four, every three by eight and every ten by one thousand and twenty four

maths_rules: slip: two folds give 2 times; true value 2 × 2 = 4
video_script.design: One idea: over any stretch of folds the thickness grows by two multiplied once for each fold. The table stays all video; two rows light up for each check; one slip at the end.

beats.on_screen: title card, From your book; the thickness table of the folded sheet for folds 0 to 10, from 0.001 cm to 1.024 cm

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.ask: the three stretches to check are listed: two folds, three folds and ten folds

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the thickness table.
<bookmark mark='table'/>In the table, each fold doubles the thickness.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many times thicker does the paper get over two folds, over three folds and over ten folds?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two rows of the table light up, an earlier thickness and a later one, with an arrow between them

marks.rows: an earlier row and a later row light up
marks.divide: the later thickness is placed over the earlier one

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Pick any two rows of the table, an earlier fold and a later fold.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>To see how many times thicker, divide the later thickness by the earlier one.

beats.on_screen: Given: the thickness table; each fold doubles the thickness

marks.given: the table and the doubling are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the thickness table, where each fold doubles the thickness.

beats.on_screen: To find: growth over 2 folds, 3 folds and 10 folds
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the growth over two folds, three folds and ten folds.

marks.one: fold three and fold five light up

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, compare fold three with fold five, which is two folds later.
Divide zero point zero three two by zero point zero zero eight.
<bookmark mark='four'/>That gives four, the same as two times two.

marks.two: fold four and fold seven light up

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, compare fold four with fold seven, which is three folds later.
Divide zero point one two eight by zero point zero one six.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>That gives eight, the same as two times two times two.

marks.three: fold zero and fold ten light up
marks.ten: 1.024 ÷ 0.001 is written, with the result left open

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, compare fold zero with fold ten, which is ten folds later.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Divide one point zero two four by zero point zero zero one.

beats.on_screen: fold 10 = 1.024 cm, fold 20 = about 1048.5 cm; 1048.5 ÷ 1.024, the same result as from fold 0 to fold 10

marks.four: fold ten and fold twenty light up
marks.same: the result is linked to the result of step three

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, start from fold ten instead, and look at fold twenty.
Fold twenty is about one thousand forty eight point five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Divide that by one point zero two four, and the result matches step three.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Two folds multiply the thickness by four.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Three folds multiply it by eight.
<bookmark mark='a10'/>Every ten folds multiply the thickness by one thousand and twenty four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the table
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: x 2 appears over two folds, then is crossed out; fold 3 to fold 4 to fold 5 shows two doublings

marks.doubt: x 2 appears over the two folds
marks.fix: x 2 is crossed out and the two doublings are drawn one after the other

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks two folds make the paper two times as thick.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But fold four doubles fold three, and fold five doubles fold four again.
Doubling twice is not the same as doubling once.
